title: Himesh Reshammiya to Headline Bollywood Music Project's 10th Anniversary in Mumbai
excerpt: The one-day festival at Jio World Garden on October 24 brings 20+ artists across two stages, with tickets from ₹1,499 on District by Zomato.
body:
• Himesh Reshammiya will headline the main stage of the Bollywood Music Project's 10th anniversary edition in Mumbai on October 24, performing a career-spanning set of his biggest hits as the festival's finale act.
  • The one-day festival at Jio World Garden features more than 20 artists across two stages — Shilpa Rao, Hariharan with son Akshay, Anu Malik's family showcase with Babul Supriyo and Shahid Mallya, Euphoria, Kutle Khan and indie acts — spanning Bollywood, folk, Sufi, indie, pop and Punjabi.
  • Tickets are on sale exclusively on District by Zomato, priced from ₹1,499 to ₹14,999 across General Access, VIP and Lounge categories; HSBC presents the edition, co-powered by Hero Vida, JBL India and Vijay Sales.
  • Last year's edition drew more than 20,000 attendees; the organisers call the 10th edition their "definitive love letter to the fans" with expanded scale and production.

A Nostalgia Headliner

Himesh Reshammiya — the composer-singer whose hooklines defined 2000s Bollywood — will close the main stage with a career-spanning set built around his biggest hits. The choice leans into the festival's anniversary theme: a decade of the Bollywood Music Project framed through the songs a generation grew up on.

"I'm really happy to be performing at The Bollywood Music Project. It's a great live celebration of Bollywood music, and I'm looking forward to bringing the audience an energetic and unforgettable evening with some of my biggest hits and lots of nostalgia."

— Himesh Reshammiya

The Lineup

The main stage opens with playback singer Anirudh Susuwaram, followed by pop act Neeraj Shridhar and a Sufi-romantic afternoon set from Roop Kumar Rathod and Sunali Rathod. Anu Malik presents a collaborative showcase with Babul Supriyo, Shahid Mallya and his daughters Anmol and Ada Malik. Euphoria joins with Vaishali Samant, Shalmali Kholgade and Abhay Jodhpurkar, while Hariharan performs alongside his son Akshay — a cross-generational pairing the singer called "a very intimate and proud moment." Shilpa Rao takes the prime-time slot ahead of the finale.

The second stage leans folk and indie: Kutle Khan's Rajasthani folk fusion, Junaid Ahmed's semi-classical set, Anjana Padmanabhan, Bombay Bandook's indie rock, Jaan Kumar Sanu, Aseem, The Qurious Band and Retro2Metro.

The Anniversary Pitch

Organiser Deepak Choudhary described the edition as the festival's "definitive love letter to the fans," promising dialled-up scale, production and sonic diversity for the landmark year. The festival adds experiential zones and curated food and beverage kiosks around the music programming.

"Ten years ago, we set out to build a boundary-breaking playground where legendary maestros, chart-topping pop icons and indie visionaries could coexist on the same stage."

— Deepak Choudhary, Organiser, Bollywood Music Project

Diaspora Angle

A decade-old Mumbai festival headlined by a 2000s nostalgia icon is exactly the kind of homeland live-music pilgrimage event that diaspora readers plan India trips around. With tickets live now on District by Zomato across three tiers, the October 24 date gives overseas fans a fixed point to book around.
